# Overview

`CALMeR` (Context-Aware Long-read MAPQ Rescuer) flags reads in long-read
transcriptome BAM files whose MAPQ is anomalously low *given* their
transcript context. It fits a Beta-Inflated (BEINF) regression model on a
sampled subset of reads, computes randomized quantile residuals on the full
table, and writes a filtered BAM plus a TSV of flagged reads.

The motivation: a uniform MAPQ threshold (e.g. `samtools view -q 30`)
disproportionately discards reads from highly multi-isoform genes,
GC-extreme transcripts, and long transcripts — not because the alignments
are low quality but because these transcript-level properties
systematically suppress MAPQ. CALMeR conditions on transcript context to
distinguish noise from biology.

# Installation

```{r install}
# CRAN deps
install.packages(c("dplyr", "readr", "ggplot2", "patchwork",
                   "data.table", "withr", "gamlss", "gamlss.dist"))

# Bioconductor deps
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages("BiocManager")
}
BiocManager::install(c("Rsamtools", "GenomicAlignments",
                       "rtracklayer", "Biostrings", "S4Vectors"))

# CALMeR (from GitHub for now; Bioconductor submission in progress)
# remotes::install_github("sparthib/CALMeR")
```

# End-to-end example

The standard pipeline is six steps. Each function corresponds to one stage:

```{r workflow}
library(CALMeR)

bam   <- "sample.sorted.bam"
gtf   <- "gencode.v46.gtf"
fasta <- "transcripts.fa"

# 1. Per-read features (MAPQ, alignment_length, plus per-transcript
#    annotation features: tx_length, n_isoforms, gc_content, pct_covered).
features <- extract_features(bam, gtf, fasta)

# 2. Standard pre-fit cleanup (primary alignments only, n_isoforms cap,
#    GC range, length range).
clean    <- clean_features(features)

# 3. Fit BEINF regression on a sample of training reads.
fit      <- fit_beinf(clean, n = 50000, seed = 42)

# 4. Score every read with a randomized quantile residual (RQR);
#    flag reads whose RQR falls below median - 3 * MAD by default.
scored   <- score_reads(features, fit,
                         filter_method = "mad", threshold = -3)

# 5. Write a filtered BAM (flagged reads removed) + a TSV of flagged
#    reads with their feature values and residuals.
filt     <- filter_bam(bam, scored,
                        out_bam = "sample_filtered.bam",
                        out_tsv = "sample_flagged.tsv.gz")

# 6. Render a diagnostic report (HTML or PDF).
calmer_report(fit, scored, out_file = "sample_report.html",
              format = "html", sample_name = "sample")
```

# Adding paralog status as an additional context predictor

When a transcript has paralogs (sequence-similar transcripts on different
genes), reads from that transcript may be ambiguously assigned even at
moderate MAPQ. `make_paralog_table()` computes per-transcript paralog
status from a `minimap2` self-alignment of the transcriptome FASTA, and
the resulting table can be joined into `extract_features()`:

```{r paralog}
# One-time per annotation: precompute paralog status. Caches the PAF for
# reuse so subsequent calls skip the alignment step.
paralog <- make_paralog_table(
    fasta    = fasta,
    gtf      = gtf,
    paf_path = "txome_self_aln.paf",   # cache PAF for reuse
    threads  = 8
)

# Per sample: extract features with paralog status joined.
features <- extract_features(bam, gtf, fasta, paralog_table = paralog)

# Fit BEINF including paralog identity as a fifth predictor.
fit <- fit_beinf(
    features,
    predictors = c("n_isoforms", "tx_length", "gc_content",
                   "pct_covered", "max_pct_id")
)
```

`make_paralog_table()` calls `minimap2` via `system2()` when a PAF doesn't
already exist; the dependency is declared in `SystemRequirements`. If
you supply a precomputed PAF (or a precomputed paralog TSV), no external
tool is needed at runtime.
